svg.desc:
Structure diagram of the wallpaper group cm on a square lattice.
Commons has no cm square variant, and unlike pm/pg this one is not the rectangular diagram with equal cell sides: cm on a square lattice puts the mirror along the cell DIAGONAL, because the centred rectangle of cm becomes square exactly when its primitive rhombus has a right angle.
Elements, in cell coordinates with the lattice generated by (312,0) and (0,312). The reflection (x,y) -> (y,x) composed with a lattice translation (a,b) is a pure reflection iff a+b = 0, giving mirror axes y = x + 312n (here the main diagonal), and otherwise a glide of vector ((a+b)/2)(1,1) about y = x + 312(n + 1/2) (here the two corner segments), the shortest being (156,156). There are no rotations. The point group has order 2, so the fundamental domain is half the cell: the two triangles either side of the mirror, drawn as the mirror image pair.
Drawn to match the public-domain Commons diagrams of this series (same palette, stroke widths and fundamental-domain corner mark) so the wall reads as one set. Released into the public domain.
